issues.detail: The Greek 'η ριζα σε' (the root [holds] you) is rendered as 'bèn là cái rễ chịu đựng ngươi'. The Vietnamese addition of 'bèn là' (then/so) and the phrasing suggests a sequential result or a new action, whereas the Greek uses 'η' (the) to identify the subject of the implied verb, creating a contrast: you hold the root, but the root [holds] you.
